title: Two brothers walk in with one message.
subtitle: Messengers of the Lord of all the worlds
then: Allah tells both brothers to go to Fir'awn and say they are {idea}messengers of the Lord of the worlds.{/idea} Ibn Kathir notes it means both of us have been sent to you. Two men from an enslaved people would say this to {trap}a king who claimed to be a god.{/trap}
now: You have to tell the landlord the repairs are not legal, or tell a senior relative the plan is wrong. You feel small in the room. {idea}What you are saying does not get its weight from your size.{/idea} Truth said gently still has its weight.
old: Who am I to say this to someone so powerful?
new: What matters is whether what I carry is true, not how big I am.
try: Say one true thing today that you have been too intimidated to say, calmly.

title: The message included a demand: let them go.
subtitle: Faith that speaks up for the oppressed
then: The second half of the message is practical. Ibn Kathir explains it as: {reward}let them go, free them{/reward} from your captivity, subjugation and torture, for they are believing servants of Allah. The Children of Israel were living in {trap}humiliating torture{/trap} under Fir'awn.
now: At work, the cleaner is shouted at and nobody says anything. In the family, one cousin is always the one blamed. {idea}Faith is not only what you believe in private.{/idea} It also asks who around you is being crushed, and whether you will speak.
old: My religion is about my prayers, not about how others are treated.
new: Standing up for someone being crushed is part of the message too.
try: Do one small thing today for someone who is usually overlooked or mistreated.

title: Fir'awn answers truth with: I raised you.
subtitle: Using past favors to silence someone
then: Fir'awn does not answer the message. He {trap}turned away and ignored him{/trap}, Ibn Kathir says, with scorn, and changed the subject: we raised you in our home and on our bed, fed you, did you favors for years. Musa grew up in Fir'awn's house.
now: You raise a concern with your boss and hear: after everything I have done for you. A parent says: I paid for your degree, so you do not get an opinion. {trap}A past favor is being turned into a gag.{/trap} Gratitude is real. So is the question that was asked.
old: If they helped me before, I have no right to disagree now.
new: I can be grateful for a favor and still say what is true.
try: Notice if you ever remind someone of your favors to win an argument. Drop it once.

title: Then he brought up the worst thing Musa ever did.
subtitle: Dragging up the past to win the present

row.title: the actual message
sub: Lord of the worlds, free them

then: Fir'awn names the killing: {trap}you did your deed{/trap}. Then the label: one of the ungrateful. Ibn Kathir says this means one who denies favors. He is still not answering the message. He is putting Musa's past on trial instead.
now: In the family argument, someone says: and what about what you did in 2019? Suddenly the real issue is gone and everyone is talking about you. {trap}Changing the subject to your past is a way to avoid the point.{/trap}
old: If they bring up my past, I have lost the argument.
new: My past can be real and the point I am making can still be true.
try: In your next disagreement, stay on the issue itself and do not bring up old faults.

title: Musa does not deny it. Yes, I did it.
subtitle: Owning a past mistake without excuses
then: Musa's answer is short. {idea}I did it then, when I was in error.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains that this was {trap}before revelation was sent{/trap} to him and before Allah made him a prophet. He does not lie, and he does not argue about it.
now: Someone brings up how you used to be. The parties, the lies, the way you treated a friend. You feel the heat rise. {idea}You can say: yes, that was me, and I was lost then.{/idea} No speech needed. It takes the weapon out of their hand.
old: I need to defend my past or hide it.
new: I can own my past honestly, because I am not who I was then.
try: Think of one past mistake you get defensive about. Say to yourself: yes, that was me then.

title: I ran. Then my Lord gave me something new.
subtitle: The past chapter closed, a new one opened
then: Musa admits he {trap}fled out of fear.{/trap} Then he points to what Allah did: {reward}granted him wisdom and made him one of the messengers.{/reward} Ibn Kathir says Musa means the first situation ended and another took its place.
now: You dropped out, lost the job, left the marriage. In your head you are still the person who ran. {reward}But Allah can turn the person who fled into the one sent back with something good.{/reward} The worst chapter does not have to be the last one.
old: The worst thing I did is who I really am.
new: Allah can close an old chapter and give me a new role.
try: Write one sentence about who you are now that your old self could not have written.

title: You raised one boy and enslaved his whole people.
subtitle: Musa weighs the favor against the harm
then: Musa turns Fir'awn's argument around. Ibn Kathir paraphrases: {idea}is there any comparison{/idea} between your favors to one man among them and {trap}the evil you have done to all of them?{/trap} The favor to Musa came out of a system that crushed his people.
now: The company gives you a bonus and a team lunch, while the contract workers are underpaid. Someone gives generously to your cause and treats their staff badly. {idea}Kindness to you does not erase harm to others.{/idea}
old: They have been good to me, so I should not question what they do to others.
new: A favor to me does not cancel injustice to many.
try: Ask yourself if loyalty to someone is keeping you quiet about how they treat others.

title: And what is this Lord of the worlds?
subtitle: Fir'awn's question was really a denial

row.title: Fir'awn
sub: I know no god but me

then: Fir'awn used to tell his people {trap}I know not that you have a god other than me{/trap}, and he fooled them into obeying. Ibn Kathir explains that his question was not curiosity about Allah's nature. He {trap}denied that the Creator existed at all{/trap}, and meant: who is this Lord besides me?
now: You ask: but why does Allah let this happen? Sometimes it is a real question and you want the answer. Sometimes it is a door you have already shut, said as a question. {idea}Ask honestly.{/idea} A question asked with a closed heart is not looking for an answer.
old: Every question I ask about faith is just honest searching.
new: A question can be a search or a wall. I should know which one I am asking.
try: Take one doubt you have and look into it today, honestly wanting the answer.

title: Musa points up, down, and everything between.
subtitle: The Lord of the heavens and the earth

row.title: a heart seeking certainty
sub: if you seek to be sure

then: Musa does not describe Allah's essence. He points to His works: {idea}the Lord of the heavens and the earth and all between them.{/idea} Ibn Kathir lists the stars, oceans, mountains, winds and birds, all {reward}submitting and humbling themselves{/reward} before Him. If you seek certainty, it is there.
now: You are stuck in traffic, staring at the brake lights. Look up: clouds moving, a bird crossing, a sky you did not make. {idea}The proof Musa gave is right outside your window.{/idea} The question is whether you want to be sure.
old: I need a clever argument before I can feel sure.
new: The heavens and earth answer the question if I really want an answer.
try: Step outside for two minutes today and look up. Just look.

title: Do you hear this? Fir'awn turns to the crowd.
subtitle: Mockery as a way to avoid answering
then: Fir'awn had no answer. Ibn Kathir says he turned to {trap}the chiefs and leaders around him{/trap} and, mocking, said: do you not hear? Meaning, are you not amazed at this man claiming {trap}you have a god other than me{/trap}?
now: Someone makes a fair point in the group chat, and instead of replying, you screenshot it to another chat with a laughing emoji. {trap}You did not answer it. You found an audience.{/trap} That is the Fir'awn move, small size.
old: If people laugh with me, I must be right.
new: Rallying an audience is not the same as having an answer.
try: Next time you disagree with someone, reply to them directly instead of mocking them to others.

title: Your Lord, and the Lord of your forefathers.
subtitle: Musa speaks to the crowd about their own origins
then: Fir'awn turned to the crowd, so Musa answers the crowd. Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}the One Who created you and your forefathers{/idea}, those who came before Fir'awn and his time. {trap}A god who was born recently{/trap} cannot be the Lord of those who lived before him.
now: The thing you treat as everything, the boss, the follower count, the career, did not exist when your grandmother was praying. It will not exist when your grandchildren are. {idea}Your Lord was Lord before all of it.{/idea}
old: What controls my life right now is what really matters.
new: Anything that came after my grandparents cannot be my Lord.
try: Call or message a grandparent or elder today and ask what they relied on in hard times.

title: Out of answers, Fir'awn calls him mad.
subtitle: Name-calling when the argument is lost
then: Fir'awn mocks the messenger as {trap}your messenger who has been sent to you{/trap}, then calls him a madman. Ibn Kathir explains Fir'awn meant there is no sense in claiming {trap}any god other than me.{/trap} The Prophet ﷺ was being called mad in Makkah too.
now: You hear it in the comments: he is crazy, she is unhinged, ignore them. Sometimes you are the one typing it. {idea}When you reach for a label instead of an answer, notice that.{/idea}
old: Calling someone crazy settles the matter.
new: An insult usually means the argument has run out.
try: Catch yourself once today before calling someone stupid or crazy, and answer their point instead.

title: Lord of the sunrise and the sunset. Can Fir'awn swap them?
subtitle: Musa calmly answers the insult with more proof
then: Called a madman, Musa does not insult back. He says {idea}Lord of the east and the west.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains: if Fir'awn is truly your lord, let him make the sun set in the east and rise in the west, like Ibrahim's challenge to the king. {reward}If you did but understand.{/reward}
now: Your cousin calls you a fanatic at the wedding. Everyone looks. You could snap back. {idea}Musa answered an insult with a sunrise.{/idea} A calm, clear reply often lands better than a sharp one.
old: When someone insults me, I have to hit back to keep my dignity.
new: Staying calm and reasonable when insulted is its own kind of strength.
try: The next time someone is rude to you, answer with one calm sentence and stop there.

title: Lose the debate, reach for the prison.
subtitle: Fir'awn turns from argument to threat
then: Ibn Kathir titles this part: after the rational proof, {trap}Fir'awn resorts to force.{/trap} When proof had been established against him clearly, he threatened prison, thinking there would be {trap}no further room for discussion.{/trap}
now: Your manager cannot answer your concern, so you get a warning about attitude. A parent loses the argument and says: as long as you live under my roof. {trap}When reasons run out, threats come in.{/trap} Notice it in others, and in your own voice too.
old: Whoever can punish me must be the one who is right.
new: Threats appear when reasons run out. Power and truth are different things.
try: When you have power over someone today, a child or a junior, give a reason instead of a threat.

title: Even if I show you something undeniable?
subtitle: Musa answers a threat with an offer
then: Threatened with prison, Musa does not panic or plead. He asks: even if I bring you {idea}something manifest{/idea}? Ibn Kathir explains this as {idea}clear and definitive proof.{/idea} Musa keeps the conversation on the truth.
now: You are told: stop bringing up the budget or you are off the team. You do not have to shout. You can say: what if I show you the numbers? {idea}A calm offer of evidence keeps the door open.{/idea}
old: When I am threatened, I either fight or go silent.
new: There is a third way: stay calm and keep offering what is true.
try: In a tense moment today, ask: can I show you why I think this?
